name: ACP PaymentManager releasePayment double release (claim tracked in memory)
summary: PaymentManager.releasePayment loads the job into memory, increments amountClaimed on that copy only and has its escrow-sufficiency check commented out, so every call pays the full job budget again out of the pooled escrow. ACPRouter releases payment automatically when a job reaches COMPLETED and also lets anyone call claimBudget on a completed job. From block 37590595 one EOA's claimBudget calls re-paid 1,408 already-settled jobs; on 2026-03-02 an attacker created a 97,000 USDC job with its own provider, completed it and claimed it a second time, and copycats followed until the implementation was replaced.

loss.notes: Each component is the USDC that PaymentManager transferred out (platform fee, evaluator fee and provider amount) in releases of a job beyond its first release: 1,865 re-releases before the attack (1,408 jobs, all sent by 0x7346dc42102b5cdba321d587564612d1f3878ad2), the attack's second 97,000 USDC release, and 49 re-releases in 7 transactions by four senders afterwards. Fees paid to the platform treasury are not deducted; the attacker's own 97,000 USDC budget, which funded the first release of its job, is not counted. USDC valued at par.

ageReset.description: UUPS upgrade of the PaymentManager proxy from its initial implementation 0x8e4fa97e4e8d0b8618065809197e1bbf4fab19ab to PaymentManager 0x56c3af6c; the next upgrade (0x536823c8, block 42834676) is the post-attack fix.

limitations: ACPRouter (proxy 0xa6c9ba866992cfd7fd6460ba912bfa405ada9df0, implementation 0x71d4d6a3f588d1ea440a5e681ecb52d53c3d255a at the anchor, later 0x7ae45990 and 0x307e34d9) supplies the two release paths (automatic release on COMPLETED and permissionless claimBudget) but holds no claim state; it is recorded as the entry point, not as a second target. Its upgrades at blocks 42827279 and 42827451 only tightened phase-jump rules (source-3 diff) and postdate the anchor.

sources.note: Reviewed root cause, first exercise, artifact identity and age history. Verified PaymentManager source (Etherscan V2 getsourcecode chainid=8453 for 0x56c3af6c, v0.8.26+commit.8a97fa7a, optimizer 200; SHA-256 of SourceCode d91c3dd102798a394811449db13d745ead627396fcb7a3a8b8ef3657e62e64c6), contracts/acp/modules/PaymentManager.sol releasePayment (onlyACP): `// require(hasSufficientEscrow(jobId, amount))` is commented out; `ACPTypes.Job memory job = IJobManager(jobManager).getJob(jobId)`; escrowDetails[jobId].releasedAmount += amount; claimableAmount = amount - job.amountClaimed; `job.amountClaimed += amount` on the memory copy; then transfers platformFee, evaluatorFee and netAmount. JobManager 0x96268da2 only sets amountClaimed = 0 at job creation, so every release pays in full. ACPRouter (verified 0x7ae45990/0x2427af51/0x307e34d9, same logic) calls _claimBudget -> paymentManager.releasePayment(job.budget) both inside the phase update when a job moves from TRANSACTION/EVALUATION to COMPLETED and from the public claimBudget(jobId) (0x91fd6372) whenever phase == COMPLETED; diffing the router sources shows its last two upgrades changed only the phase-jump condition. First exercise: eth_getLogs PaymentReleased(uint256,address,uint256,address,string) (topic 0xfcf126c1...) on the PaymentManager proxy, blocks 36786082..42900000 in adaptive windows: 1,714,356 events over 1,712,441 jobs; 1,412 jobs have more than one release and for all of them eth_call escrowDetails(jobId) shows releasedAmount > amount. The earliest is job 1000011800: automatic release in 0xdbb08c0d83efe340ed1debabdcc3083cd671dc1e70a1aabd6b7df6d6954ebeb1 (block 37590590, log 332, 6000 to provider 0x5b5852b8c772e388b71c106440df4e1bb53467ae), then source-1 (block 37590595, index 217): EOA 0x7346dc42102b5cdba321d587564612d1f3878ad2 calls router claimBudget(1000011800) and the PaymentManager transfers 4000 + 6000 USDC base units again (logs 500/501, PaymentReleased log 502). No earlier job was released twice. Sender 0x7346dc42 is a claimBudget keeper EOA, not the attacker: Etherscan V2 txlist shows it calling claimBudget (0x91fd6372) on the previous ACP contract 0x6a1fe26d54ab0d3e1e3168f2e0c0cda5cc0a0a4a from block 32328728, all 40 transactions it sent in blocks 37590127..37590883 are claimBudget on the router or 0x6a1fe26d, and eth_getTransactionCount is 689908 at latest. Its re-claims are non-malicious exercises of the same defect that moved other jobs' escrowed USDC to non-entitled recipients, so the first of them is the anchor. The attack (source-5, block 42832267, index 16) creates job 1002573889 funded with 97000 USDC, reaches COMPLETED (release log 149) and claims it again (log 152). Age: EIP-1967 Upgraded logs on the proxy up to the attack are 36786082 (construction, 0x8e4fa97e) and source-2 (block 37251864, index 296, log 515, topic1 0x56c3af6c); later upgrades begin at 42834676. Implementation slot 0x3608...2bbc reads 0x8e4fa97e at 37251863 and 0x56c3af6c at 37251864 and 37590594. Implementation 0x56c3af6c is a top-level creation in 0x18147bfdc6ac4dec6c4641e9ad46adc7c4bba093690f78fbca5a4fbaddd2a059 (block 37251847, index 186, by 0xc31cf1168b2f6745650d7b088774041a10d76d55); eth_getCode is 0x at 37251846 and keccak256 0x96eb314359995fd6377c06a7af7dc05cf1648f48d2465182e6a815227842c740 at 37251847, 37590594 and 42832266. The proxy (runtime keccak256 0xee8a105971995661291a9f284262a87abf2381b3cdc93b2c8fbeffe4cd636dd9 at 36786082 and 37590594, empty at 36786081) is a top-level creation in source-8 (index 115) by 0x9547e85f3016303a2996271314bde78b02021a28. The flaw depends on no configuration value, so the implementation activation supplies the age.

Reviewed loss. For every job with more than one PaymentReleased event, each release after the first was matched in its receipt to the ERC-20 Transfer logs from the PaymentManager proxy that precede that PaymentReleased log (back to the previous one): 1,915 re-releases in 1,873 transactions, all USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913 (6 decimals). Before the attack: 1,865 re-releases, 1,408 jobs, blocks 37590595..42832181, all sent by 0x7346dc42, 2889850000 base units. Attack source-5: 97000000000 (second release of job 1002573889: 19400 USDC fee to 0xe9683559a1177a83825a42357a94f61b26cd64c1 plus 77600 USDC to attacker provider 0xc1ee502dd42bb5433b3fc7b153c9334255fc3c07, logs 150/151). After the attack: 49 re-releases in 7 transactions by 0x6bc22cd3705b86c1d423d80001721b9c8101d2e1 (37), 0x46c403e3dcaf219d9d4de167ccc4e0dd8e81eb72 (6), 0x7346dc42 (4) and one other, blocks 42832332..42832928 (last source-7), 2607700000 base units; none later before the fix at 42834676 (scan to 42900000). Total 102497.55 USDC. Cross-check: sum over the 1,412 jobs of escrowDetails releasedAmount - amount is 102861.14 USDC; the 363.59 difference sits in 24 jobs whose releasedAmount also counts refundBudget bookkeeping, which transfers nothing from the PaymentManager, so the transfer-based figure is used.
Native USDC on Base valued at USD 1 par at each component's timestamp.
